pages.title: Lease failover
pages.markdown:
# Lease failover

## Recovery
To preserve acknowledged writes after an owner fails, first fence the old owner. Wait for its lease to expire, replay the committed journal on a replica, acquire a higher ownership epoch, and then resume writes. Never accept two owners for the same object.

pages.title: Restart a node
pages.markdown:
# Restart a node

Check process health and restart the daemon. This process checklist does not transfer ownership or establish that writes are durable. Follow the lease failover procedure when an owner is unavailable.

pages.title: Backup recovery
pages.markdown:
# Backup recovery

## Restore an older snapshot
Use this procedure to recover an earlier state after an accidental deletion. Stop writes, select a snapshot from before the deletion, restore it, and inspect the recovered data before resuming. Changes after that snapshot are absent.

pages.title: Concurrent edits
pages.markdown:
# Concurrent edits

## Merge a stale draft
If an update returns 412, read the current page and its revision. Preserve your draft, compare both versions, merge the intended changes, and submit with the new If-Match revision. Do not blindly retry a stale replacement.

pages.title: Sharing access
pages.markdown:
# Sharing access

The complete wiki URL contains a secret fragment. Anyone holding it can read, edit and delete the wiki. Share the full link only with intended participants. Names on edits and comments are self-reported.

pages.title: Chat retention
pages.markdown:
# Chat retention

Transient chats expire after their configured idle interval. Accepted posts refresh that interval; reads do not. Persistent wikis have a separate lifecycle and are not deleted when a chat expires.

pages.title: Browser cache
pages.markdown:
# Browser cache

An HTTP cache stores response bytes. This is unrelated to restoring a storage snapshot or recovering ownership of a failed node. Authenticated wiki responses use no-store.

pages.title: Planning notes
pages.markdown:
# Planning notes

The team discussed node failure, recovery, leases, backup storage, concurrent edits and sharing. This agenda records topics only; it contains no recovery or editing procedure.
